Guide to discharge or modify restrictive covenants
HMLR Practice Guide 62A rights to light/air
official_measurement_examples: Upper Tribunal restrictive-covenant guidance was updated 14 July 2026
restrictive covenant is a private land-use restriction and is distinct from planning control
title register may set out covenant wording or refer to a filed deed
a register restriction is not the same legal concept as a restrictive covenant
planning permission does not automatically discharge a restrictive covenant
section 84 procedure can be used to seek discharge or modification where statutory grounds are met
presence of an old covenant does not by itself prove current enforceability without benefit/burden and factual analysis
covenant status does not establish ownership infrastructure capacity or final development yield
core_rules: restrictive covenant is not planning policy
planning permission does not override private covenant
title summary is not full covenant wording
historic age does not automatically extinguish covenant
Upper Tribunal application is not discharge order
discharge order is not planning permission
covenant does not prove access rights
covenant does not calculate development yield
no parcel covenant clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official HMCTS Upper Tribunal, HM Land Registry, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. 14 July 2026 tribunal guidance currentity retained; no parcel promotion.
